name: Nested decorative borders
summary: Separate nested elements with background steps, spacing and type instead of drawing a border around each level.
problem: Every extra outline asks for attention. When a bordered container holds bordered cards, inputs and buttons, nothing is the boundary that matters and the interface turns into a grid of boxes.

bad.description: A bordered panel contains a bordered card, which contains a bordered input and bordered buttons.

good.title: Elevation, not outlines
good.description: One panel on a lighter surface. Inputs and buttons are filled one step lighter than their parent. No border anywhere.

why: Hierarchy is carried by the dark to light surface ramp, spacing and type weight. A border is kept for the rare boundary that is meaningful, so it still means something when it appears.
exceptions: A single outline around an overlay (menu, dialog, popover) is allowed: it separates floating content from whatever sits behind it. The content inside stays borderless.

Checkboxes, radios and similar controls whose shape must be perceivable may keep their own outline even inside a container (WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 non-text contrast). Prefer a fill step first and add the outline only when the fill cannot reach the contrast.
Data grids may draw cell dividers; use hairline dividers, not boxes, and not on every cell edge.

humanReview: Does a bordered element sit inside another bordered element?
Is the remaining border marking a boundary a user needs, or only proving the element exists?
